name: Traceability Matrix - IDM
rows: The Accountable Authority determines their entity's tolerance for security risks and documents in the security plan.
Identity and access decisions must align to NDIA's approved security risk tolerance and be represented in the security plan.
Supporting - applies to identity risk acceptance, IAM exceptions and control design for all NDIA digital identity populations.

Identity and access controls, deviations and residual risks must be assessed against NDIA's approved security risk tolerance, documented, owned and escalated through the security governance process before approval.
A risk steward (or manager) is identified for each security risk or category of security risk, including shared risks.
IAM risks are shared across business, ICT, cyber, personnel security and third-party service owners and require named stewardship.
Supporting - applies to identity lifecycle risks, privileged access risks, federated access and third-party access administration.

NDIA must assign accountable owners or stewards for identity lifecycle risks, including joiner/mover/leaver, privileged access, federation, provider and partner access, and participant identity assurance.
The Accountable Authority considers the impact that their security risk management decisions could potentially have on other entities, and shares information on risks where appropriate.
Identity federation, external access and shared services can create security risks for other entities and service providers.
Supporting - applies where NDIA shares identity services, authentication decisions, federated access or identity risk information.
NDIA must consider and share material identity and access risks with affected entities, partners and service providers where NDIA authentication, federation or access decisions could affect them.
Third-party, procurement, supplier and cloud identity governance

The entity is accountable for the management of security risks arising from procuring goods and services and ensures procurement and contract decisions do not expose the entity or the Australian Government to an unacceptable level of risk.
Third parties may create, manage, support or use digital identities that access NDIA systems and information.
Direct - applies to contractors, partners, providers, managed service providers and any third party with NDIA system access.

Procurement and contract decisions for services involving NDIA identity stores, access administration, federated access or system support must include an identity and access risk assessment. Unacceptable identity and access risks must not be accepted without approved treatment.
Third-party, procurement, supplier and cloud identity governance

Procurement, contracts and third-party outsourced arrangements contain proportionate security terms and conditions to ensure service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements.
Contracts need enforceable terms for identity proofing, account management, MFA, privileged access, logging and offboarding.
Direct - applies to all outsourced services, contractors, subcontractors, partners and providers requiring NDIA digital access.

Contracts and third-party arrangements must include identity and access security obligations proportional to the service, including unique accounts, MFA, least privilege, timely offboarding, incident notification, audit rights and compliance with PSPF and ISM controls.
Third-party, procurement, supplier and cloud identity governance
Entity ensures service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements as detailed by the entity.
Service providers may operate identity controls or access NDIA information and must comply with NDIA-mandated security requirements.
Direct - applies to third parties and subcontractors with NDIA system access or IAM responsibilities.

NDIA must require service providers, contractors and subcontractors with NDIA system access or IAM responsibilities to comply with NDIA identity and access controls and provide assurance evidence when requested.
Identity incident, breach response and notification

Contractual security terms and conditions require service providers to report any actual or suspected security incidents to the entity, and follow reasonable direction from the entity arising from incident investigations.
Identity compromise, credential misuse and unauthorised access are security incidents that require prompt reporting and direction.
Direct - applies to third parties operating, administering or using NDIA identities, credentials or access control services.

Contractual terms must require providers to notify NDIA of actual or suspected identity, credential, authentication, authorisation or access-control incidents and comply with NDIA incident directions.
Third-party, procurement, supplier and cloud identity governance

Contract security terms and conditions are monitored and reviewed to ensure the specified security controls, terms and conditions are implemented, operated and maintained by the contracted provider, including any subcontractors, over the life of a contract.
Third-party identity controls must be monitored and evidenced throughout the contract life, not only at onboarding.
Direct - applies to ongoing assurance of supplier access, subcontractor access and provider/partner integrations.

NDIA must periodically monitor, review and evidence the operation of contracted identity controls, including privileged access, federated access, account recertification, logs, offboarding and subcontractor access.
Third-party, procurement, supplier and cloud identity governance
Contractual terms and conditions include appropriate security arrangements for the completion or termination of the contract.
Contract completion or termination must include a controlled exit for accounts, credentials, tokens, trusts and entitlements.
Direct - applies to all third-party and contractor identities and service integrations at contract completion or termination.

NDIA must define completion and termination procedures for third-party access, including disabling accounts, revoking credentials and tokens, removing federation trusts, returning assets, and confirming access logs and records are retained.
Third-party, procurement, supplier and cloud identity governance
Procurement and contract decisions consider the security risks before engaging providers operating under foreign ownership, control or influence.
Foreign ownership, control or influence can increase risk where providers administer identities or access NDIA systems.
Supporting - applies to third-party services that administer identities, provide identity tooling or access NDIA systems.

Before using providers subject to foreign ownership, control or influence for identity services or access to NDIA systems, NDIA must assess identity, privileged-access and data-access risks and obtain required security approvals.
Third-party, procurement, supplier and cloud identity governance
Security risks arising from contractual arrangements for the provision of goods and services are managed, reassessed and adjusted over the life of a contract.
Identity and access risks change as contracts, subcontractors, integrations, hosting arrangements and threat conditions change.
Direct - applies to all third-party access arrangements over the contract lifecycle.
NDIA must reassess and adjust identity controls over the life of a contract when service scope, users, subcontractors, integrations, hosting, threat environment or security classifications change.
Third-party, procurement, supplier and cloud identity governance
Secure and verifiable third-party vendors, providers, partners and associated services are used unless business operations require use, and the residual risks are managed and approved by the CISO.
IDM depends on trusted and verifiable vendors, providers, partners and supporting services.
Direct - applies to identity platforms, integration services, managed service providers, partners and provider access services.

NDIA must use secure, verifiable third-party identity vendors, providers, partners and associated services. Where business operations require otherwise, residual identity and access risks must be formally accepted by the CISO or delegate.
Information classification, protected Agency information and lawful access

The value, importance or sensitivity of official information is assessed by the originator by considering the potential damage to the government, the national interest, organisations or individuals that would arise if the information's confidentiality were compromised.
Access rights must reflect the value, importance and sensitivity of information accessed through NDIA systems.
Direct - applies to role-based and attribute-based access design, entitlement approval and access review.
Access control rules must be based on the value, sensitivity and potential harm of NDIA information, including participant data, official information and any classified or caveated material.
Information classification, protected Agency information and lawful access
The minimum protections and handling requirements are applied to protect OFFICIAL and security classified information.
Minimum protections and handling requirements determine the strength of authentication, authorisation and monitoring controls.
Direct - applies to access to OFFICIAL and security classified information through NDIA systems.

NDIA identity controls must enforce minimum protections for OFFICIAL and security classified information, including authentication strength, authorisation, audit logging, session management and access review appropriate to the classification.
Information classification, protected Agency information and lawful access
The Australian Government Security Caveat Standard and special handling requirements imposed by the controlling authority are applied to protect security caveated information.
Security caveats impose access restrictions that must be enforced through identity attributes, roles and approvals.
Conditional - applies where NDIA systems hold or provide access to caveated information.

Where NDIA systems hold caveated information, access must be limited to identities meeting caveat controlling authority requirements. Authorisation must reflect caveat rules, citizenship or clearance constraints and explicit need-to-know.
Information classification, protected Agency information and lawful access
Apply the Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard's 'Rights' property where the entity wishes to categorise information content by the type of restrictions on access.
Metadata expressing access restrictions supports reliable authorisation decisions and auditability.
Supporting - applies to systems capable of metadata-driven access control or recordkeeping integration.

Where NDIA systems use recordkeeping or information management metadata to categorise access restrictions, IAM controls must consume or respect the Rights property or equivalent metadata to support access decisions and audit.
Information classification, protected Agency information and lawful access

Access to security classified information or resources is only provided to people outside the entity with the appropriate security clearance (where required) and a need-to-know, and is transferred in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements.
External access to classified information requires clearance and need-to-know before an identity can be authorised.
Conditional - applies to people outside NDIA who require digital access to security classified information or resources.

NDIA must only grant external digital access to security classified information or resources to identities with the required clearance, verified need-to-know and approved transfer and handling arrangements.
Information classification, protected Agency information and lawful access
An agreement or arrangement is in place before security classified information or resources are disclosed or shared with a person or organisation outside of government.
Identity or federated access cannot be used to share classified information outside government without an approved arrangement.
Conditional - applies where NDIA enables access for persons or organisations outside government to classified resources.

Before enabling identity or federated access for a person or organisation outside government to classified NDIA resources, NDIA must have an approved agreement or arrangement defining access scope, controls, responsibilities and termination.
Information classification, protected Agency information and lawful access

Australian Government security classified information or resources bearing the AUSTEO caveat is never shared with a person who is not an Australian citizen, even when an international agreement or arrangement is in place, unless an exemption is granted.
AUSTEO imposes citizenship-based access limits that must be enforceable through IAM attributes and approval records.
Conditional - applies where NDIA systems handle AUSTEO information or resources.
IAM rules for AUSTEO material must prevent access by non-Australian citizens unless a valid approved exemption is recorded and access is explicitly authorised.
Information classification, protected Agency information and lawful access
Australian Government security classified information or resources bearing the AGAO caveat is not shared with a person who is not an Australian citizen, except as specified.
AGAO caveats impose citizenship and controlling authority restrictions that must be reflected in authorisation rules.
Conditional - applies where NDIA systems handle AGAO information or resources.
IAM rules for AGAO material must prevent access by non-Australian citizens except where the PSPF and controlling authority permit it, and the decision is recorded.
Identity platform, application and infrastructure security
The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual controls and cyber security guidelines are applied on a risk-based approach.
Identity platforms, directories, authentication services and access-control integrations are technology systems subject to ISM controls.
Direct - applies to identity stores, directories, IAM tooling, federation, authentication, authorisation and logging services.

NDIA must design, configure and operate identity platforms, directories, federation services, authentication services, privileged access tools and access-control integrations using ISM controls and risk-based cyber security guidelines.
Authentication, MFA, credentials, recovery and sessions
Multi-factor authentication mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
MFA is a mandatory cyber mitigation that directly strengthens identity assurance and prevents credential compromise.
Direct - applies to privileged, remote, workforce and high-risk external access; participant and provider authentication as risk assessed.

NDIA must implement MFA to at least Essential Eight Maturity Level Two for applicable accounts and systems, prioritising privileged, remote, administrative, staff, contractor, partner and provider access, with participant-facing MFA applied in accordance with risk, usability and legislative requirements.
Restrict administrative privileges mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Administrative privileges create elevated risk and require stronger controls than standard user access.
Direct - applies to all administrative, privileged, break-glass and service administration accounts.

NDIA must restrict administrative privileges using least privilege, unique named admin accounts, time-bound or just-in-time elevation where available, separation of duties, MFA, logging, monitoring and periodic recertification.
Identity proofing, verification, assurance, eligibility and authority
The eligibility and suitability of personnel who have access to Australian Government people and resources is ensured.
Digital access must not be granted until eligibility and suitability assurance exists for personnel accessing government resources.
Direct for staff and contractors; conditional for partners/providers with NDIA resource access; not applicable to participants as personnel screening.

NDIA must verify that workforce and third-party personnel are eligible and suitable before creating or enabling digital access to NDIA resources. Participant identities must use risk-based identity proofing appropriate to the participant service.
Identity proofing, verification, assurance, eligibility and authority
The pre-employment screening identity check is conducted for all personnel, to verify identity to at least Level 3 (High) of Assurance of the National Identity Proofing Guidelines.
Personnel identity proofing establishes confidence that the person receiving a digital identity is the intended person.
Direct for staff, contractors and personnel identities; informs assurance levels for provider and participant identities.

Before granting staff, contractor or other personnel access, NDIA must verify identity to at least Level 3 (High) of the National Identity Proofing Guidelines, or apply a documented risk-based equivalent for non-personnel digital identities.
Identity proofing, verification, assurance, eligibility and authority
Biographic information in identity documents is verified to ensure the information matches the original record.
Credential issuance and account activation depend on verified identity evidence, not self-asserted identity data.
Direct for personnel onboarding; risk-based for provider, partner and participant identities.

NDIA must verify biographic information in identity evidence against authoritative records before issuing or activating workforce credentials, privileged accounts or other high-assurance digital identities.
Identity proofing, verification, assurance, eligibility and authority
The pre-employment screening eligibility check is conducted for all personnel, to confirm their eligibility to work in Australia and for the Australian Government.
Work eligibility determines whether personnel can receive employment-linked access to NDIA systems and resources.
Direct for staff and contractors; not applicable to participant accounts except where separate legislative eligibility rules apply.
NDIA must confirm work eligibility and Australian Government work eligibility requirements before granting personnel accounts or access rights that rely on employment or engagement status.
Identity proofing, verification, assurance, eligibility and authority
The entity obtains assurance of each person's suitability to access Australian Government resources during pre-employment screening.
Suitability assurance is a prerequisite for access to government resources and should be visible to access approvers.
Direct for workforce personnel; conditional for providers and partners with government resource access.

NDIA must obtain and record suitability assurance before granting identities access to NDIA resources, and access approvers must be able to verify suitability status when authorising accounts or roles.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
Prior to granting temporary access to security classified information or resources, pre-employment checks are completed.
Temporary digital access cannot bypass required pre-employment checks for access to classified resources.
Conditional - applies to temporary access to security classified information or resources.
Temporary identities or access for classified NDIA resources must not be enabled until required pre-employment checks are completed and recorded, unless an approved PSPF exception applies.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
A risk assessment determines whether a person is granted temporary access to security classified information or resources.
Temporary access requires an explicit risk assessment covering access scope, duration, controls and withdrawal triggers.
Conditional - applies to temporary access to security classified information or resources.

NDIA must complete and record a security risk assessment before granting temporary access to security classified information or resources, including access scope, duration, supervision, controls and withdrawal triggers.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
Temporary access to security classified information, resources and activities is supervised.
Supervision and monitoring reduce the risk of temporary access to classified information or activities.
Conditional - applies to temporary access to security classified information, resources or activities.
Temporary access to classified information, systems or activities must be supervised, monitored and logged, with a named accountable sponsor and clearly defined access duration.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions

Short-term temporary access to security classified information, resources and activities is limited to the period in which an application for a security clearance is being processed, or up to a total combined maximum of three months in a 12-month period.
Short-term temporary access must be limited and cannot become an uncontrolled standing entitlement.
Conditional - applies to short-term temporary access while security clearance processing is underway.
Short-term temporary access must be limited to the permitted clearance-processing period or the PSPF maximum and must expire automatically unless a new approval is recorded.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions

The Authorised Vetting Agency confirms that the completed security clearance pack has been received, and that no initial concerns have been identified, before short-term temporary access is changed to provisional temporary access.
Provisional access depends on assurance from the Authorised Vetting Agency before access is expanded.
Conditional - applies to provisional temporary access to security classified information or resources.

NDIA must not convert short-term temporary access to provisional access until the Authorised Vetting Agency has confirmed receipt of the completed clearance pack and no initial concerns are identified.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
Temporary access to classified caveated information, resources or activities is not granted, other than in exceptional circumstances, and only with the approval of the caveat controlling authority.
Caveated resources require exceptional approval and cannot be accessed temporarily through standard IAM approvals.
Conditional - applies to temporary access to classified caveated information, resources or activities.
Temporary access to caveated information, systems or activities must be blocked by default and only enabled in exceptional circumstances with caveat controlling authority approval recorded.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
Prior to granting temporary access, the entity obtains an undertaking from the person to protect the security classified information, resources and activities they will access.
Access undertakings create enforceable obligations for temporary users before identities are enabled.
Conditional - applies before temporary access to security classified information, resources or activities.

Before temporary access is granted, NDIA must obtain the user's undertaking to protect the classified information, resources and activities they will access, and record the undertaking with the access approval.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions

Prior to granting temporary access, the entity obtains agreement from any other entity (or third party) whose security classified information, resources and activities will be accessed by the person during the temporary access period.
Agreement is required where temporary access includes another entity's or third party's classified resources.
Conditional - applies where temporary access includes classified information, resources or activities owned by another entity or third party.
Where temporary access includes another entity's or third party's classified information, systems or activities, NDIA must obtain the relevant agreement before provisioning access.
Access lifecycle, least privilege, role design and segregation of duties
Access to official information is facilitated for entity personnel and other relevant stakeholders.
The identity lifecycle is the mechanism for granting authorised access to official information for personnel and stakeholders.
Direct - applies to entity personnel and relevant stakeholders including contractors, partners and providers.

NDIA must provide authorised access to official information for personnel and relevant stakeholders through managed identity lifecycle processes that are timely, auditable and based on approved business need.
Access lifecycle, least privilege, role design and segregation of duties
Appropriate access to official information is enabled, including controlling access (including remote access) to supporting technology systems, networks, infrastructure, devices and applications.
NDIA must control access to systems, networks, infrastructure, devices and applications, including remote access.
Direct - core IAM requirement for all NDIA digital identity populations.

NDIA must control digital access, including remote access, to systems, networks, infrastructure, devices and applications through approved identity, authentication, authorisation, monitoring and deprovisioning controls.
Access lifecycle, least privilege, role design and segregation of duties
Access to security classified information or resources is only given to entity personnel with a need-to-know that information.
Need-to-know is an authorisation principle that constrains access to classified information and should influence role design.
Conditional - applies to security classified information and resources; the least-privilege principle applies more broadly.
Access to security classified NDIA information or resources must be limited to identities with a verified need-to-know and approved role or entitlement; broader access must be avoided.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
Personnel requiring ongoing access to security classified information or resources are security cleared to the appropriate level.
Ongoing classified access requires a valid clearance at the appropriate level before access is provisioned or retained.
Conditional - applies to ongoing access to security classified information or resources.
NDIA must ensure identities requiring ongoing access to security classified information or resources have a current clearance at the required level before provisioning or retaining access.
Information classification, protected Agency information and lawful access
Personnel requiring access to caveated information meet any clearance and suitability requirements imposed by the originator and caveat controlling authority.
Caveated access has additional clearance, suitability and controlling authority conditions that IAM must enforce.
Conditional - applies to access to caveated information and resources.
NDIA must ensure identities requiring caveated information meet clearance and suitability conditions set by the originator or controlling authority before access is granted or retained.
Authentication, MFA, credentials, recovery and sessions

A unique user identification, authentication and authorisation practice is implemented on each occasion where system access is granted, to manage access to systems holding security classified information.
Unique identification, authentication and authorisation are core identity controls for granting system access.
Direct - core requirement for NDIA IAM across staff, contractors, partners, providers and participants.

NDIA must use unique user identifiers, strong authentication and explicit authorisation each time system access is granted. Shared accounts are prohibited except where formally approved, risk assessed and technically controlled.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
A security risk assessment of the proposed location and work environment informs decisions by the CSO to allow personnel to work in another government entity's facilities in Australia.
Location and work environment risks affect whether remote or facility-based access should be enabled.
Supporting - applies where IAM enables access from another government entity's Australian facilities.

Where NDIA enables personnel to access NDIA systems from another government entity's Australian facilities, the access decision must reflect the CSO-informed risk assessment of the location and work environment.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
An agreement is in place to manage the security risks associated with personnel working in another government entity's facilities in Australia.
Inter-entity facility access requires an agreement covering identity, access, monitoring and withdrawal responsibilities.
Supporting - applies where personnel access NDIA systems while working in another government entity's Australian facilities.
NDIA must have an agreement defining identity, access, monitoring, incident and withdrawal responsibilities before enabling access for personnel working from another government entity's facilities.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
Approval for remote access to TOP SECRET information, data or systems in international locations is only granted if approved by the Australian Signals Directorate.
Remote access to TOP SECRET information from international locations has stringent approval requirements.
Conditional - applies only to TOP SECRET international remote access scenarios.

NDIA must not enable remote digital access to TOP SECRET information, data or systems from international locations unless ASD approval has been obtained and identity controls enforce the approved conditions.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
A security risk assessment of the proposed location and work environment informs decisions to allow personnel to work remotely in international locations.
International remote access creates additional identity, device, jurisdiction and information risks.
Supporting - applies to international remote access requests; conditional where classified information is involved.

NDIA must risk assess international remote access requests before provisioning access, including user identity assurance, device posture, location, data classification, monitoring and revocation arrangements.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions

Personnel are not granted approval to work remotely in locations where Australian Government information or resources are exposed to extrajudicial directions from a foreign government that conflict with Australian law, unless operationally required.
Some locations expose users and data to foreign government direction that may conflict with Australian law.
Supporting - applies to international remote access and high-risk locations.

NDIA must not approve or enable remote access from locations where Australian Government information or resources may be subject to conflicting extrajudicial foreign direction unless operationally required and risk accepted.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
The AGSVA or the TOP SECRET-Privileged Access Vetting Authority is used to conduct security vetting.
Clearance status used for access decisions must originate from an authorised vetting authority.
Conditional - applies where access requires a security clearance.
NDIA identity processes must rely on AGSVA or the TOP SECRET-Privileged Access Vetting Authority outcomes for clearance-dependent access, rather than locally substituting vetting decisions.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
The gaining sponsoring entity establishes new clearance conditions before assuming sponsorship of an existing security clearance that is subject to clearance conditions.
Transferred clearances with conditions must be established and reflected before access is granted.
Conditional - applies when NDIA assumes sponsorship of a clearance subject to conditions.

When NDIA assumes sponsorship of a clearance with conditions, identity and access administrators must not grant clearance-dependent access until the new clearance conditions are established and recorded in access rules.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions

The gaining sponsoring entity undertakes the exceptional business requirement and risk assessment provisions prior to requesting transfer of sponsorship of an existing security clearance that is subject to an eligibility waiver.
Eligibility waivers increase access risk and require exceptional business need and risk assessment before transfer of sponsorship.
Conditional - applies when NDIA seeks transfer of a clearance subject to an eligibility waiver.

Before NDIA assumes sponsorship of a clearance subject to an eligibility waiver, the identity process must verify that exceptional business need and risk assessment requirements have been completed and any access limits are recorded.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
Positions that require a security clearance are identified and the level of clearance required is documented.
Role and position clearance requirements drive whether an identity can be provisioned to sensitive roles or systems.
Direct for workforce role design; conditional for systems or roles requiring classified access.

NDIA must identify positions and system roles that require a security clearance and record the required clearance level so provisioning rules can prevent access by uncleared or under-cleared identities.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
Each person working in an identified position has a valid security clearance issued by the relevant Authorised Vetting Agency.
Clearance validity must be checked before clearance-dependent access is provisioned or retained.
Conditional - applies to personnel in roles requiring a valid security clearance.
NDIA must verify that each person in a clearance-required position has a valid clearance issued by the relevant Authorised Vetting Agency before access is granted or retained.
Identity proofing, verification, assurance, eligibility and authority
Australian citizenship is confirmed and pre-employment screening is completed before the entity seeks a security clearance for a person.
Citizenship and pre-employment screening are prerequisites before clearance-dependent access is sought or enabled.
Supporting - applies to personnel onboarding prior to clearance-dependent access.
NDIA must confirm Australian citizenship and complete required pre-employment screening before seeking a security clearance and before granting access that depends on a clearance outcome.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
The Sponsoring Entity establishes an exceptional business need and conducts a risk assessment before a citizenship eligibility waiver is considered for a non-Australian citizen.
A citizenship eligibility waiver requires exceptional business need and risk assessment before it can support an access pathway.
Conditional - applies to non-Australian citizens needing clearance-dependent access.

For non-Australian citizens requiring clearance-dependent access, NDIA must verify that exceptional business need and risk assessment requirements are satisfied before any access pathway relying on a citizenship eligibility waiver is progressed.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
The Accountable Authority (or the CSO if delegated) approves a citizenship eligibility waiver and maintains a record of all citizenship eligibility waivers approved.
Citizenship eligibility waivers must be approved and recorded before they are relied on for access decisions.
Conditional - applies where clearance-dependent access relies on a citizenship eligibility waiver.
NDIA must not provision clearance-dependent access relying on a citizenship eligibility waiver unless approval by the Accountable Authority or delegated CSO is recorded and available for audit.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
The Sponsoring Entity establishes an exceptional business need and conducts a risk assessment before a checkable background eligibility waiver is considered.
Checkable background eligibility waivers affect access risk and require exceptional business need and risk assessment.
Conditional - applies where clearance-dependent access may rely on a checkable background eligibility waiver.
Where a checkable background eligibility waiver is considered for clearance-dependent access, NDIA must verify exceptional business need and a risk assessment before access can be considered.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
The Sponsoring Entity's Accountable Authority (or the CSO if delegated) approves checkable background eligibility waivers and maintains a record of all such waivers approved.
Checkable background eligibility waivers must be approved and recorded before supporting clearance-dependent access.
Conditional - applies where clearance-dependent access relies on a checkable background eligibility waiver.

NDIA must not provision clearance-dependent access relying on a checkable background eligibility waiver unless approval by the Accountable Authority or delegated CSO is recorded and access conditions are applied.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
The Sponsoring Entity actively assesses, monitors and manages the ongoing suitability of personnel.
Ongoing suitability can change after access is granted and must trigger access review when relevant.
Direct for workforce and third-party access; conditional for participant or provider accounts through risk-based monitoring.

NDIA must continually monitor and manage suitability signals relevant to digital access and ensure identity status, role changes, conduct concerns and security advice trigger access review, restriction or withdrawal.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
The Sponsoring Entity monitors and manages compliance with any conditional security clearance requirements and reports any non-compliance to the Authorised Vetting Agency.
Clearance conditions must be translated into access constraints and monitored for compliance.
Conditional - applies to personnel with conditional clearance requirements.

NDIA must monitor compliance with conditional clearance requirements and report non-compliance to the Authorised Vetting Agency. Access must be adjusted, suspended or withdrawn where conditions affect system access.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions
The Sponsoring Entity monitors and manages compliance with security clearance maintenance obligations for the clearance holders they sponsor.
Clearance maintenance obligations affect whether a clearance holder remains eligible for access.
Conditional - applies to clearance holders sponsored by NDIA.
NDIA must monitor clearance maintenance obligations for sponsored clearance holders and ensure failure to meet obligations prompts access review and, where required, restriction or suspension.
Access lifecycle, least privilege, role design and segregation of duties
The CSO, CISO (or other relevant security practitioner) is advised prior to separation or transfer of any proposed cessation of employment resulting from misconduct or other adverse reasons.
Adverse separation or transfer can require accelerated access risk treatment and security practitioner involvement.
Direct - applies to staff, contractors and third-party workforce identities.

NDIA HR, contract management and business owners must notify the CSO, CISO or relevant security practitioner before adverse separation or transfer so identity access can be risk assessed, monitored and withdrawn at the right time.
Access lifecycle, least privilege, role design and segregation of duties
A risk assessment is completed to identify any security implications in situations where it is not possible to undertake the required separation procedures.
If normal leaver procedures cannot occur, access risk must still be assessed and treated.
Direct - applies to exceptional separation, abandonment, urgent termination or inaccessible-account scenarios.

Where normal separation procedures cannot be completed, NDIA must complete a security risk assessment and apply compensating identity controls, including immediate account suspension, credential revocation, monitoring and asset or data recovery steps.
Access lifecycle, least privilege, role design and segregation of duties
Separating personnel have their access to Australian Government resources withdrawn upon separation or transfer from the entity.
Withdrawing or adjusting access at separation, transfer or relationship change is a core identity lifecycle control.
Direct - core joiner/mover/leaver requirement for workforce and third-party identities; applies to providers and participants when access relationship changes.

NDIA must withdraw or adjust access to Australian Government resources immediately upon separation, transfer, contract completion, role change or loss of business need, including disabling accounts, revoking tokens and removing entitlements.
Access lifecycle, least privilege, role design and segregation of duties
The Sponsoring Entity advises the relevant Authorised Vetting Agency of the separation of a clearance holder, including any relevant circumstances.
Vetting authority notification affects clearance sponsorship and clearance-dependent access records.
Conditional - applies to clearance holders sponsored by NDIA.

For separating clearance holders, NDIA must notify the relevant Authorised Vetting Agency of separation and relevant circumstances, and ensure clearance sponsorship changes are reflected in identity and access records.
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions

The Sponsoring Entity ensures clearance subjects with an eligibility waiver or where a waiver is being considered, are not given temporary or provisional access to security classified information or resources until the security vetting process is complete.
Eligibility waivers cannot justify temporary or provisional classified access before vetting is complete.
Conditional - applies where an eligibility waiver is being considered or has been granted.

Where an eligibility waiver is being considered or has been granted, NDIA must prevent temporary or provisional access to security classified information or resources until the security vetting process is complete.
Access lifecycle, least privilege, role design and segregation of duties
ISM Cyber Security Principle PRO-13 - Identity, credential and access management
Robust and secure identity, credential and access management establishes, maintains and controls access and supports detection of misuse.
This is the central control objective for an ICT identity policy.
Applies to every NDIA user, customer, provider, partner, service account, device, certificate and AI agent identity.
NDIA must maintain a controlled identity, credential and access management capability that uniquely identifies entities, verifies access authority and detects misuse.
Australian Government Information Security Manual controls and guidance
Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)
Access lifecycle, least privilege, role design and segregation of duties
ISM Cyber Security Principle PRO-12 - Least privilege
Access privileges should be limited to the minimum required to perform authorised functions.
Least privilege is necessary for role-based access, segregation of duties and zero-trust enforcement.
Applies across workforce, participant support, provider functions, administrators, service accounts and AI agents.
Access must be limited to the minimum systems, data and actions required for the approved purpose and must be removed when no longer required.
Australian Government Information Security Manual controls and guidance
Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)
Authentication, MFA, credentials, recovery and sessions
ISM - Guidelines for system hardening: authentication hardening
